data.narrative:
Inertia Enterprises is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Jeff Lawson, Annie Kritcher, and Mike Dunne that has raised $450M to date. The Climate & Energy sector comprises 9 peer companies—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private—including peers such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

The valuation analysis employs a stage-progression method, the only applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. This method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression to the $450M total raised as a valuation proxy, yielding an implied value of $900M. A peer-median approach is not applicable: while 9 same-sector peers exist, insufficient datapoints meet narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier peers), and applying an all-sector median would lack explanatory power for this specific company.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $765M to $1.0B, centered at $900M. This range reflects the stage-progression framework and incorporates typical valuation dispersion around the point estimate. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for this particular company's capital efficiency and market position, the representativeness of total raised as a valuation proxy absent confirmed prior round prices, and the absence of comparable-stage peer data to validate or adjust the implied step-up. Investors should condition any reliance on this range on direct diligence into unit economics and market traction.
